haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits the write and outbox row first, then copies inline to Postgres. A Postgres failure never fails the client; the relay retries later.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version. Missing rows are inserted; otherwise the row is left alone.
haiku-low.q3: Every running instance must report users.dual_write=1, held at least 30 seconds, and 10 minutes must pass since confirmation. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: It reads the MySQL replica, not the primary, in 2000-id batches. It pauses while replica lag exceeds 5 seconds, and one advisory-lease worker runs.
haiku-low.q5: Reads need a clean comparator pass and under 60s outbox backlog, then 1/10/50/100% stages. The source switch needs a 3-day soak at 100% and a passing readiness check.
haiku-low.q6: The outbox row records it: users_outbox in MySQL, or pg_outbox after the switch, written in the same transaction. The relay applies it until success, and the comparator backs it up.
haiku-low.q7: Every copy takes a per-id lock and checks the users_erased tombstone. Deletes insert the tombstone under the same lock, so a late copy is blocked.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is last_completed_id in Postgres users_backfill_progress, committed atomically with each batch. It stops when a batch returns fewer than 2000 rows.
haiku-low.q9: Comparator checksums rows. Missing or older Postgres rows are copied; Postgres-only rows are deleted with a tombstone; newer Postgres versions page a human.
haiku-low.q10: MySQL fence closes, then the outbox drains, then Postgres opens, so they never overlap. If not drained by T+45, the watchdog aborts and reopens MySQL.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids from users_id_seq, set at switch above MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT plus 1,000,000. Copies insert ids, raising MySQL's counter, so rollback cannot reuse them.
haiku-low.q12: MySQL stays a mirror via the reverse relay for 14 days; rollback is a fenced, drained switch back. It ends when mirroring stops at step 13.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first (transaction with fence, write, outbox row; commit), then an inline copy to Postgres with 300 ms timeout. If Postgres fails the caller still sees success (no error); the outbox row stays for the relay. Client waits at most 300 ms extra.
sonnet.q2: Only if the row is missing, or the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version (version rule: WHERE users.version < EXCLUDED.version). Also blocked if the id is in users_erased.
sonnet.q3: Step 4's gate: the count of instances with app_flag_value{flag="users.dual_write"}=1 must equal the running instance count; then at least 10 minutes since dual_write_confirmed_at, and mysql_replica_lag_seconds below 5. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds (cache refresh every 30s; normally gate met within ~35s).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica rather than the primary, in batches of 2000 ids, and before each batch checks replica lag; if lag is above 5 seconds it sleeps and rechecks, reading nothing. One backfill worker runs under an advisory lease.
sonnet.q5: Reads: step 6 has a clean comparator pass (zero persistent mismatches, zero repairs), then stages 1, 10, 50, 100% at least 1 hour each, with low Postgres read errors/fallback rate, p99 within target, nightly comparator clean. Source of truth switch: soak at 100% reads for at least 3 days (72h), and step 9 readiness: comparator pass with zero mismatches within 24h, both outbox ages small, mirror_to_mysql=true set, reverse relay healthy, switch script rehearsed in staging including abort path.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_outbox in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the write, holding op and full row_json) records it. The MySQL-to-Postgres relay, a dedicated worker, reads rows in seq order, applies them with copy_to_pg (retrying with backoff), and deletes the row after success. Alert fires if oldest row is over 5 minutes.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: the users_erased table in each database. Every copy runs in a transaction that first takes a per-id lock (Postgres advisory xact lock on hash(id)%256 stripes; MySQL SELECT ... FROM users_erased FOR SHARE), then checks users_erased and skips erased ids. The delete path inserts the tombstone and deletes the row under the same lock, so order doesn't matter. Backfill also skips ids in users_erased, and waits 10 minutes for deletes before the flag landed.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres table users_backfill_progress (last_completed_id, run_id). The progress update is in the same Postgres transaction as the batch upsert, so they commit or roll back together; on restart it resumes at last_completed_id. It stops when a batch returns fewer than 2000 rows, which marks the backfill complete.
sonnet.q9: The comparator, which walks the id space in 2000-id chunks comparing row checksums on the MySQL replica vs Postgres. Mismatches are rechecked after 60s against the MySQL primary; if an outbox row exists for the id it is skipped until a later pass. Persistent ones: missing/older version in Postgres -> copy_to_pg; in Postgres but absent in MySQL and not in users_erased -> delete from Postgres and add tombstone; newer version in Postgres than MySQL -> page a human and stop (a bug).
sonnet.q10: Fences (users_control accepting_writes per database, taken FOR SHARE by every write). Close MySQL's fence and set writer=postgres, drain users_outbox, set the sequence, then open Postgres's fence; both are closed in between, so stale or new-flag instances get 503 only. If it runs long, the watchdog aborts if Postgres is not open by T+45: re-opens MySQL, sets flag back to mysql, Postgres never accepted a write; pause ends by about T+75, under 90 s.
sonnet.q11: Postgres, from users_id_seq. Before opening, setval to GREATEST(MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, max(id) in Postgres, current value) + 1,000,000. The copy inserts the id explicitly into MySQL, raising its AUTO_INCREMENT counter, so after a rollback to MySQL ids are not reused.
sonnet.q12: Writes go Postgres-first, with pg_outbox written in the same transaction and copied to MySQL inline (300 ms) or by the reverse relay (version rule, MySQL tombstones), so MySQL is a live mirror for 14+ days. Rollback (step 12, only before step 13, when pg_outbox age under ~10s): close Postgres fence, set writer=mysql, drain pg_outbox to MySQL, open MySQL; pause at most 90 s, watchdog aborts on failure. The option ends at step 13 (after 14 days, clean comparator, empty pg_outbox, sign-off): mirror_to_mysql=false, reverse relay stopped, MySQL write grants revoked; rollback is then impossible.
